chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Sa'id ibn Janah, from some of our companions, from al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said:

"Indeed, Abu al-Khattab had corrupted the majority of the people of Kufa, and they would not pray the Maghrib prayer until the twilight (shafaq) disappeared. And that is only for the traveler, the one fearing danger, and the one with a need."

key_terms.الشَّفَقُ: Twilight, the reddish glow in the sky after sunset
key_terms.الْخَائِفِ: The one fearing (danger or safety concerns)
key_terms.صَاحِبِ الْحَاجَةِ: The one with a need (a specific concession for necessity)
key_terms.لِلْمُسَافِرِ: For the traveler (implying a concession for travel)

ai.seo_question: When is it permissible to delay the Maghrib prayer until twilight disappears?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies that the people of Kufa, led by Abu al-Khattaw, erroneously generalized the concession for travelers and the anxious to the entire community, thereby distorting the standard time for Maghrib prayer. This narration highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that delaying prayer until the disappearance of red twilight (ghurub al-shafaq) is a specific exception (rukhsa) rather than the default obligation (asl), emphasizing the importance of adhering to the precise times established by the Ahl al-Bayt.
